notes: Foundational taxonomy for the MVP. Terms are controlled: a classification may only reference a term defined here. Synonyms feed the rule-based intent parser; they are matched as whole phrases.

dimensions.label: Genre
dimensions.description: Conventional form/genre labels. Necessary for filtering, deliberately not the main discovery signal.

dimensions.label: Theme & subject
dimensions.description: What the work is about: ideas, questions and subject matter it substantively engages with (not merely mentions).

dimensions.label: Mood & experience
dimensions.description: The felt experience of engaging with the work. Multidimensional: a work can be comforting and melancholic at once.

dimensions.label: Pacing
dimensions.description: How quickly the work moves and how much patience it asks of its audience.

dimensions.label: Complexity & demand
dimensions.description: How much attention, interpretation or prior knowledge the work asks for.

dimensions.label: World & setting
dimensions.description: Qualities of the setting and world-building.

dimensions.label: Style & craft
dimensions.description: Visual, sonic, prose or interactive style.

dimensions.label: Content advisory
dimensions.description: Content some people want to avoid; the basis of each work's parents' guide. Strength encodes intensity: 0 = assessed and absent, 0.3 = mild/brief, 0.6 = notable, 0.9 = graphic/central. A missing row means NOT ASSESSED, never 'absent'. Each term belongs to one guide group.

terms.label: Science fiction
terms.definition: Speculation grounded in science, technology or plausible-seeming extrapolation.

terms.label: Fantasy
terms.definition: Worlds or events governed by magic, myth or the impossible, presented without scientific rationale.

terms.label: Drama
terms.definition: Primarily character- and situation-driven, played straight.

terms.label: Horror
terms.definition: Designed primarily to frighten, disturb or create dread.

terms.label: Thriller
terms.definition: Organised around suspense, danger and escalating stakes.

terms.label: Romance
terms.definition: A romantic relationship is the central narrative concern.

terms.label: Comedy
terms.definition: Primarily intended to amuse.

terms.label: Mystery
terms.definition: Structured around uncovering hidden facts: a crime, a puzzle or a secret.

terms.label: Historical
terms.definition: Set in, and substantively engaged with, a real historical period.

terms.label: War
terms.definition: Armed conflict is the setting and central concern.

terms.label: Animation
terms.definition: A screen work made wholly or chiefly through animation.

terms.label: Literary fiction
terms.definition: Fiction foregrounding prose, character interiority and theme over genre convention.

terms.label: Adventure
terms.definition: Journeys, exploration and discovery drive the experience.

terms.label: Action
terms.definition: Physical conflict, pursuit and spectacle drive the experience.

terms.label: Puzzle
terms.definition: Progress depends chiefly on solving logical or observational problems.

terms.label: Role-playing game
terms.definition: Player shapes a character's abilities and choices over a long arc.

terms.label: Metroidvania
terms.definition: Interconnected map gated by abilities acquired over time.

terms.label: Life / farming sim
terms.definition: Everyday routines, cultivation and community as the core loop.

terms.label: Ambient
terms.definition: Music prioritising atmosphere and texture over melody or rhythm.

terms.label: Jazz
terms.definition: Music in the jazz tradition.

terms.label: Rock
terms.definition: Music in the rock tradition, including alternative rock.

terms.label: Electronic
terms.definition: Music made primarily with electronic instruments and production.

terms.label: Post-rock
terms.definition: Rock instrumentation used for texture and long-form dynamics rather than song form.

terms.label: Folk / indie folk
terms.definition: Acoustic, song-centred music in folk traditions.

terms.label: Art pop
terms.definition: Pop song forms pursued with experimental ambition.

terms.label: Language & communication
terms.definition: How meaning is made and shared; translation, misunderstanding, the limits of language.

terms.label: Time & causality
terms.definition: Time travel, loops, non-linear perception or the nature of time itself.

terms.label: Grief & loss
terms.definition: Mourning, bereavement, and living with absence.

terms.label: Memory
terms.definition: Remembering, forgetting and the reliability of the past.

terms.label: Identity & selfhood
terms.definition: What makes a self: continuity, authenticity, who one is.

terms.label: Consciousness & artificial minds
terms.definition: Machine intelligence, synthetic life, or what it means to be conscious.

terms.label: Isolation & solitude
terms.definition: Physical or emotional aloneness as a central condition.

terms.label: First contact & the alien
terms.definition: Encounter with an intelligence or phenomenon radically unlike us.

terms.label: Class & inequality
terms.definition: Economic and social hierarchy and its consequences.

terms.label: Surveillance & authoritarianism
terms.definition: State control, surveillance, censorship and complicity.

terms.label: War & its human cost
terms.definition: The experience and consequences of war for individuals.

terms.label: Love & connection
terms.definition: Romantic love, intimacy or deep human connection.

terms.label: Nature & ecology
terms.definition: The natural world, ecosystems and humanity's place within them.

terms.label: Coming of age
terms.definition: Transition from childhood or youth to maturity.

terms.label: Everyday life & routine
terms.definition: The texture and meaning of ordinary days.

terms.label: Politics & social systems
terms.definition: Ideologies, political systems and how societies organise themselves.

terms.label: Mortality & meaning
terms.definition: Death, finitude and the search for meaning or purpose.

terms.label: Duty, restraint & regret
terms.definition: Lives shaped by obligation, repression or missed chances.

terms.label: Race & the legacy of slavery
terms.definition: Racial injustice and the historical legacy of slavery.

terms.label: Gender & sexuality
terms.definition: Gender roles, gender identity and sexuality as subjects.

terms.label: Power, empire & religion
terms.definition: Imperial power, messianism and the manipulation of belief.

terms.label: Knowledge & curiosity
terms.definition: The pursuit of understanding; science, scholarship and the urge to know.

terms.label: Kindness & community
terms.definition: Decency, care and belonging as central forces.

terms.label: Technology & alienation
terms.definition: Modern life, technology and consumerism as sources of estrangement.

terms.label: Decay & impermanence
terms.definition: Erosion, entropy and things passing away.

terms.label: Contemplative
terms.definition: Invites reflection; leaves room to think.

terms.label: Melancholic
terms.definition: Wistful sadness that is felt but not crushing.

terms.label: Comforting
terms.definition: Restorative and safe; leaves you feeling better.

terms.label: Tense
terms.definition: Sustained suspense or anxiety.

terms.label: Eerie
terms.definition: Uncanny, strange and quietly unsettling.

terms.label: Uplifting
terms.definition: Hopeful; leaves the audience with optimism.

terms.label: Bleak
terms.definition: Dark and largely without consolation.

terms.label: Whimsical
terms.definition: Playful, fanciful, lightly magical.

terms.label: Romantic
terms.definition: Tender and swooning; the feeling of falling for someone.

terms.label: Exhilarating
terms.definition: High energy and adrenaline.

terms.label: Sense of wonder
terms.definition: Awe at the scale or strangeness of the world or universe.

terms.label: Funny
terms.definition: Reliably makes you laugh.

terms.label: Unsettling / disturbing
terms.definition: Leaves lasting discomfort or dread.

terms.label: Slow burn
terms.definition: Unhurried; rewards patience.

terms.label: Brisk
terms.definition: Moves quickly; little downtime.

terms.label: Intellectually demanding
terms.definition: Rewards close attention and interpretation; ideas carry weight.

terms.label: Easy to get into
terms.definition: Low barrier to entry; enjoyable without effort.

terms.label: Non-linear structure
terms.definition: Events presented out of chronological order by design.

terms.label: Time loop
terms.definition: A repeating span of time is the structural engine.

terms.label: Unreliable narrator
terms.definition: The telling cannot be fully trusted, and this matters to the meaning.

terms.label: Puzzle-box narrative
terms.definition: The audience must actively piece together what is happening.

terms.label: Environmental storytelling
terms.definition: Story told through places, objects and traces rather than exposition.

terms.label: Minimal or no dialogue
terms.definition: Communicates largely without words.

terms.label: Meaningful choices
terms.definition: Player decisions materially shape outcomes.

terms.label: Dialogue-driven
terms.definition: Conversation carries most of the story.

terms.label: Concept / narrative album
terms.definition: An album organised around a unifying story or concept.

terms.label: Rich world-building
terms.definition: A detailed, internally coherent invented world with history and systems.

terms.label: Grounded realism
terms.definition: A recognisable real world, closely observed.

terms.label: Space & other worlds
terms.definition: Set substantially in space or on other planets.

terms.label: Mythic & folkloric
terms.definition: Draws on myth, folklore or spirits as a living framework.

terms.label: Atmospheric
terms.definition: Mood and sense of place are primary craft achievements.

terms.label: Visually striking
terms.definition: Distinctive imagery is central to the experience.

terms.label: Hand-drawn
terms.definition: Hand-drawn animation or art.

terms.label: Minimalist
terms.definition: Spare, restrained use of means.

terms.label: Lyrical prose
terms.definition: Prose valued for its beauty and rhythm.

terms.label: Low-budget ingenuity
terms.definition: Made on small means, with inventiveness substituting for budget.

terms.label: Graphic violence
terms.definition: On-screen or described violence depicted explicitly.

terms.label: Body horror
terms.definition: Disturbing transformation or violation of the body.

terms.label: Sexual content
terms.definition: Depicted or explicitly described sexual activity or nudity.

terms.label: Atrocity & mass death
terms.definition: Depiction of massacre, genocide or mass death.

terms.label: Jump scares & horror intensity
terms.definition: Sudden frights or sustained horror intensity.

terms.label: Strong language
terms.definition: Swearing and crude or offensive language.

terms.label: Alcohol, drugs & smoking
terms.definition: Depicted or described use of alcohol, drugs or tobacco.

terms.label: Suicide & self-harm
terms.definition: Depiction, discussion or implication of suicide, suicidal thoughts or self-harm.

terms.label: Crime
terms.definition: Built around crimes, criminals or those who pursue them.

terms.label: Documentary
terms.definition: Non-fiction film or television about real people and events.

terms.label: Family
terms.definition: Made for all ages to enjoy together.

terms.label: Musical
terms.definition: Story told substantially through song and dance.

terms.label: Biography
terms.definition: Tells the story of a real person's life.

terms.label: Superhero
terms.definition: Costumed heroes with extraordinary powers.

terms.label: Western
terms.definition: Set on a frontier, usually the American West, with its codes and violence.

terms.label: Sports
terms.definition: Centred on a sport, its contests and those who play it.

terms.label: Non-fiction
terms.definition: Factual writing about real events, people or ideas.

terms.label: Memoir
terms.definition: A first-person account of the author's own life.

terms.label: Popular science
terms.definition: Explains science or how the world works for general readers.

terms.label: Graphic novel
terms.definition: A story told in comics form, at book length.

terms.label: Hip-hop
terms.definition: Rap and beat-driven music from hip-hop culture.

terms.label: Pop
terms.definition: Melodic, hook-driven popular music.

terms.label: Classical
terms.definition: Western art music, orchestral or chamber, of any period.

terms.label: R&B & soul
terms.definition: Rhythm and blues, soul and their descendants.

terms.label: Metal
terms.definition: Heavy, distorted, amplified guitar music.

terms.label: Indie rock
terms.definition: Guitar music from independent or alternative scenes.

terms.label: Punk
terms.definition: Fast, raw, anti-establishment rock.

terms.label: Soundtrack & film music
terms.definition: Music written for or drawn from films, series and games.

terms.label: Singer-songwriter
terms.definition: Personal songs, often sparse, centred on voice and lyric.

terms.label: Global traditions
terms.definition: Music rooted in a regional or traditional idiom outside Anglo-American pop.

terms.label: Strategy
terms.definition: Winning through planning and resource management.

terms.label: Shooter
terms.definition: Combat centred on aiming and shooting.

terms.label: Platformer
terms.definition: Movement and jumping across obstacles is the core challenge.

terms.label: Roguelike
terms.definition: Repeated runs through changing levels, with permanent loss on failure.

terms.label: Racing
terms.definition: Competing for speed in vehicles.

terms.label: Stealth
terms.definition: Avoiding detection is the main way through.

terms.label: Family
terms.definition: Parents, children and siblings, and the ties and strains between them.

terms.label: Crime & justice
terms.definition: What drives crime, and what justice and punishment really mean.

terms.label: Revenge
terms.definition: Retribution and its cost.

terms.label: Survival
terms.definition: Staying alive against nature, enemies or collapse.

terms.label: Heroism & sacrifice
terms.definition: Courage, duty, and giving something up for others.

terms.label: Migration & diaspora
terms.definition: Leaving home, arriving elsewhere, and living between cultures.

terms.label: Mental health
terms.definition: Depression, anxiety, trauma and recovery, treated seriously.

terms.label: Ambition & money
terms.definition: Success, greed, status and what people trade for them.

terms.label: Nostalgic
terms.definition: A warm or aching pull toward the past.

terms.label: Darkly funny
terms.definition: Humour found in grim, absurd or taboo places.

terms.label: Epic
terms.definition: Grand in scale and stakes; sweeping.

terms.label: Ensemble cast
terms.definition: Many protagonists share the story.

terms.label: Anthology
terms.definition: Separate stories collected around a theme or format.

terms.label: Open world
terms.definition: A large world you can roam freely, in any order.
